Hostel applicants should plan for a separate application and an uncertain allocation, while day scholars should compare their commute against the actual department timetable.

The current handbook describes classrooms, laboratories, multimedia theatres, a library, indoor stadium-cum-auditorium, open-air theatre, hostels, clinic and canteens. Student associations and co-curricular activities complement the academic programme; availability of specific facilities should be checked with the relevant department.

The handbook describes the Centre for Life Frontier Engagement, a Career Guidance and Placement Centre and opportunities such as service-learning and summer internship activity. Course requirements vary: applicants should ask their department which fieldwork, project or internship components belong to their specific award before budgeting for travel or external training.

Hostels are part of the campus facilities. The current admission instructions require a separate hostel application after submitting a course application and expressly state that applying does not guarantee admission to a hostel. Hostel and mess charges should be confirmed separately from the academic fee tables.

The handbook identifies canteens and refreshment corners. It does not establish a current special-diet or allergy-accommodation commitment; applicants should check menus, mess arrangements and any individual requirements with the college before moving in.

A clinic, counselling services and student-welfare arrangements are documented. The counselling centre describes individual support and wellbeing activities; these services should not be presented as a guarantee of personal safety or specialist treatment.

The official material describes counselling, a Career Guidance and Placement Centre and student-support structures. Applicants with non-standard or overseas qualifications must obtain the required eligibility decision rather than assuming automatic equivalence.
